newsitem.title: USA: US spot LPGs stable to weaker in thin trade.
newsitem.headline: US spot LPGs stable to weaker in thin trade.

text.p: U.S. liquefied petroleum gas prices were stable to weaker in light activity late on Tuesday as players stood back to assess which direction the market may take.
"We are sort of in an interim period between the end of winter season and the beginning of summer season," said a Houston-based broker.
"People aren't willing to take positions yet," the broker added.
Meanwhile, the butane market drifted a tad lower in the U.S. Gulf Coast amid the expected arrival of an Algerian butane cargo over the weekend to Enterprise.
Another cargo is expected to arrive next weekend.
The asking price for Belvieu, Texas, normal butane dipped a quarter cent to 44.25 cents and a 5,000 barrel isobutane deal traded for 50.00 cents, traders said.
Belvieu spot propane was unchanged and the bid price for Conway material slipped a quarter cent. ((--Laney Salisbury, New York Energy Desk 1212 859-1631))
